correctness.rationale: The sixth-character indicator on the nonzero coset χ(x)=−1 has 6 terms; expanding three consecutive positions yields 125 supported-three terms bounded by 2sqrt(p), 75 supported-two terms bounded by sqrt(p)+1, and 15 supported-one terms bounded by 2. Hence 216N(p)>=p−325sqrt(p)−108. Positivity at 106000 is strict by integer-square comparison; the function increases thereafter. An independently written Euler-criterion verifier, not using the submitted primitive-root generator, exhausts all 5,044 eligible primes below 106000, finding exactly the stated 28 exceptions ending at 1399. This establishes the prime-field classification when combined with the cited Weil bound; it does not address proper extension fields.
